drhp.business: Jeyyam Global Foods sources, processes and supplies pulse-based products, with principal products chana, fried gram and besan. It operates predominantly in a single reportable business segment comprising the processing and sale of chana and chana-based food products, serving institutional and trade customers and progressively strengthening its branded consumer-facing portfolio.
drhp.end_markets: institutional customers|trade customers|urban, semi-urban and emerging regional centres (branded/retail)
drhp.expansion: The Company is progressing the Gulbarga facility, positioned closer to major raw-material sourcing centres, with potential to improve procurement efficiency and reduce inward logistics costs. Capital work-in-progress reflects ongoing investment associated with manufacturing capacity, and the Company's near-term priorities include stabilising and utilising new capacity alongside greater automation and process improvement across manufacturing operations. The Company also sees opportunity to expand into value-added categories such as spices, ready-to-cook products and allied pulse-based foods.

sk.overview: India is the world's largest milk producer, contributing ~26% of global milk production in CY25, and the Indian dairy market is stated at INR 12.0T in FY26 within a packaged food market of INR 15.8T and an F&B market of INR 74.0T. Milk and value-added dairy products (VADP) together account for ~76% of the packaged food market, with liquid milk at INR 5.9T and VADP at INR 6.1T in FY26; VADP is stated to represent ~51-52% of the dairy market and to grow faster than milk (12.4% vs 7.8% CAGR FY26-31). risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Seasonality, crop output, climatic events, imports, regulation and commodity-price volatility can affect availability and gross margins; raw materials represent a substantial portion of the Company's cost base.
- High receivables and supplier advances may lengthen the cash-conversion cycle and increase dependence on short-term funding.
- Food-safety, product-quality, labelling and statutory non-compliance can result in financial and reputational consequences.
- Customer concentration, delayed collections or supplier performance issues can affect liquidity and operations.
- Plant breakdown, process failure, cyber incidents or interruption of critical systems may disrupt production and reporting.
- Margins are inherent to commodity-oriented products, and scaling higher-margin branded products will take time.
- Competition from organised brands, regional processors and unorganised market participants.
- Risks relating to new capacity, product launches, distribution expansion and brand investment.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Consolidate the core business, improve capacity utilisation, maintain financial discipline and increase the contribution from branded and value-added products.
- Strengthen the 'Jeyyam' brand and gradually expand presence beyond the traditional business-to-business segment, widening market reach of branded chana, besan and fried gram.
- Pursue greater automation and process improvement across manufacturing operations to enhance productivity, consistency and food-safety/quality standards.
- Strengthen the distribution network.
